GUIDANCE ANALYSIS: Home Depot — Q4 2025

METRIC: Total sales growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 2.5% to 4.5% growth
UNIT: percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Total reported sales growth.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Reflects contributions from the GMS acquisition, new stores, branches and tuck-in acquisitions.
- Housing affordability, historically low housing turnover, consumer economic uncertainty, inflation, job concerns and higher financing costs are expected to continue pressuring demand.

METRIC: Comparable sales growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately flat to 2% growth
UNIT: percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Company comparable sales growth.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects housing and home-improvement demand pressures to persist because it has not seen a catalyst for an inflection in housing activity.
- Cited pressures include the mortgage-rate environment, elevated home prices, historically low housing turnover, inflation, job concerns and higher financing costs.

METRIC: Market share
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Company market share.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management expects to continue growing market share in any environment.
- The company attributes this outlook to strengthening its competitive position and delivering the best customer experience, including investments in stores, interconnected shopping and Pro capabilities.

METRIC: Housing and home-improvement demand
GUIDANCE TYPE: Qualitative
NUMERICAL GUIDANCE: None stated; use management rationale only
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Industry housing and home-improvement demand environment.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management anticipates that housing and home-improvement demand pressures will persist and said it has not yet seen a catalyst for an inflection in housing activity.
- Headwinds cited were the current mortgage-rate environment, significant home-price appreciation since 2019, historically low housing turnover, inflation, job concerns and higher financing costs.

METRIC: SRS organic sales growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: mid-single-digit percent organic sales growth
UNIT: percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: SRS organic sales growth.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management intends to support SRS's momentum.

METRIC: New Home Depot stores
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 15 new stores
UNIT: stores
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Planned Home Depot store openings.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Part of the company's planned growth investments.

METRIC: New SRS locations
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: 40-50 new SRS locations
UNIT: locations
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Planned SRS-location openings.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Part of management's plan to support SRS momentum and expansion.

METRIC: Gross margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 33.1%
UNIT: percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: GAAP gross margin.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- No specific forward gross-margin driver was provided with the fiscal 2026 target.

METRIC: Operating margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 12.4% to 12.6%
UNIT: percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: GAAP operating margin.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- No specific forward operating-margin driver was provided with the fiscal 2026 target.

METRIC: Adjusted operating margin
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 12.8% to 13.0%
UNIT: percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Non-GAAP adjusted operating margin, excluding intangible asset amortization.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- No specific forward adjusted-operating-margin driver was provided with the fiscal 2026 target.

METRIC: Effective tax rate
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately 24.3%
UNIT: percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Effective tax rate.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- No specific forward tax-rate driver was provided with the fiscal 2026 target.

METRIC: Net interest expense
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately $2.3 billion
UNIT: USD billions
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: Reported net interest expense.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- No specific forward net-interest-expense driver was provided with the fiscal 2026 target.

METRIC: Diluted earnings per share growth
GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately flat to 4% growth compared to fiscal 2025
UNIT: percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026
TIMEFRAME SCOPE: Full Year
BASIS: GAAP diluted earnings per share; compared with fiscal 2025 diluted EPS of $14.23.
MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- The outlook reflects the fiscal 2026 sales, demand and margin assumptions.
- Housing and home-improvement demand pressures are expected to persist.

GUIDANCE TYPE: Quantitative
PROJECTION/GUIDANCE: approximately flat to 4% growth compared to fiscal 2025
UNIT: percent
TIMEFRAME/TARGET PERIOD: Fiscal 2026

- The outlook reflects the fiscal 2026 sales, demand and margin assumptions.

MAIN RATIONALE/DRIVERS:
- Management plans to continue investing in the business.

COMPARABLE EARNINGS ANALYSIS: Home Depot — Q1 2026
STRICT REPORT WINDOW: 2026-04-04 to 2026-05-18

COMPARABLE: Floor & Decor Holdings, Inc. (FND)
REPORT DATE: 2026-04-30
REPORTED PERIOD: Q1 fiscal 2026 (13 weeks ended 2026-03-26)
WHY COMPARABLE: A public specialty retailer of hard-surface flooring, installation materials and decorative accessories. It shares Home Depot exposure to homeowner and professional repair-and-remodel projects, big-ticket discretionary project deferral, housing turnover and consumer confidence. It is included because the release directly attributes its first-quarter demand outcome to those shared macro conditions, rather than merely being another home-related retailer.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Big-ticket repair-and-remodel demand
- Mortgage rates and housing turnover
- Consumer sentiment and gasoline-price pressure
- Professional and DIY project activity
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Elevated 30-year mortgage rates, higher gasoline prices and weaker consumer sentiment reduced demand for big-ticket discretionary purchases. [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Floor & Decor said these conditions produced a challenging demand environment and first-quarter earnings weaker than it had anticipated. Comparable-store sales declined 3.7%, net sales declined 0.7% to $1,152.3m, operating income declined 18.4%, and diluted EPS declined 17.8% to $0.37.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is a negative but attenuated read-through for Home Depot's larger-ticket discretionary project categories. Home Depot has substantially broader maintenance, repair and pro demand, so the specialty flooring comparable-sales decline should not be copied directly.
  SOURCE: https://ir.flooranddecor.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/296/floor-decor-holdings-inc-announces-first-quarter-fiscal
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://ir.flooranddecor.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/296/floor-decor-holdings-inc-announces-first-quarter-fiscal
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://ir.flooranddecor.com/news-events/ir-calendar/detail/8947/q1-2026-earnings-conference-call

COMPARABLE: Masco Corporation (MAS)
REPORT DATE: 2026-04-22
REPORTED PERIOD: Q1 2026 (three months ended 2026-03-31)
WHY COMPARABLE: Masco supplies directly overlapping home-improvement categories, including Behr paint, Delta faucets, bath fixtures and decorative hardware. Its release and call provide category-specific evidence on North American plumbing, professional paint and DIY paint demand, as well as tariff and commodity-cost pressure that can transmit to Home Depot through shared suppliers and retail categories.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- North American repair-and-remodel demand
- DIY paint demand
- Professional paint and plumbing demand
- Tariff and commodity costs
- Retail price realization
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- North American plumbing demand and pricing were positive, while DIY paint demand was softer. [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Plumbing Products sales rose 9% reported and 7% in local currency; the call attributes 6 percentage points of plumbing growth to pricing and says volume was slightly positive. North American plumbing sales rose 9% in local currency. In Decorative Architectural Products, professional paint sales grew mid-single digits while DIY paint sales declined low single digits; total Decorative Architectural Products sales were flat.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The slightly positive plumbing volume and strong pricing support Home Depot's plumbing and pro-related categories, but the low-single-digit DIY paint decline is a modest negative read-through for DIY discretionary project activity. The net signal is mixed, so only the explicitly weak DIY-paint component is used in the comparable-sales adjustment.
  SOURCE: https://s21.q4cdn.com/596588259/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/transcript/MAS-Q1-2026-Transcript.pdf
  SOURCE: https://investor.masco.com/news-stream/news-details/2026/Masco-Corporation-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx
- Higher tariff and commodity costs offset part of price and cost-savings benefits. [INDUSTRY, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Masco reported adjusted operating-profit growth of 13% and adjusted operating-margin expansion of 90 basis points. On its call, it stated that pricing actions and cost savings drove profit but were partially offset by higher tariff and commodity costs.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This indicates input-cost pressure in overlapping home-improvement categories, but Masco's manufacturer price realization, cost structure and sourcing differ from Home Depot's retail gross-margin model. It therefore informs caution on EPS/margin but provides no defensible per-share Home Depot adjustment.
  SOURCE: https://s21.q4cdn.com/596588259/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/transcript/MAS-Q1-2026-Transcript.pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://investor.masco.com/news-stream/news-details/2026/Masco-Corporation-Reports-First-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://investor.masco.com/events-and-presentations/event-details/2026/Masco-Corporation-2026-First-Quarter-Conference-Call/default.aspx
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://s21.q4cdn.com/596588259/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/transcript/MAS-Q1-2026-Transcript.pdf

COMPARABLE: The Sherwin-Williams Company (SHW)
REPORT DATE: 2026-04-28
REPORTED PERIOD: Q1 2026 (three months ended 2026-03-31)
WHY COMPARABLE: Sherwin-Williams has direct exposure to paint and coatings demand across professional, DIY and retail channels, including product categories sold at Home Depot. Its Paint Stores same-store-sales result is a useful, though pro-skewed, indicator for repair-and-remodel paint demand; its input-cost commentary also bears on overlapping coatings supply chains.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Paint and coatings demand
- Professional repair-and-remodel activity
- DIY project activity
- Raw-material and petrochemical input costs
- Retail pricing
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- Demand remained soft in most end markets, but Paint Stores same-store sales increased. [MACRO, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Sherwin-Williams characterized the quarter as having continued demand softness in most end markets. Nevertheless, Paint Stores Group sales increased 3.7% and same-store sales increased 2.4%; consolidated sales increased 6.8% to $5.67bn. The company attributed performance in part to growth investments, new accounts and share-of-wallet gains.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The positive paint same-store-sales result is a modest positive read-through for Home Depot's paint and pro customer activity. It is heavily attenuated because Sherwin-Williams' dedicated-store model, account gains and pro mix are not equivalent to Home Depot's total-company comparable sales.
  SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-First-Quarter-Financial-Results/
- Raw-material costs moderated in Q1, while oil, natural-gas and petrochemical costs subsequently inflated and became volatile. [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Sherwin-Williams stated that higher income before tax in Q1 was aided by moderating raw-material costs. On the earnings call, it said oil, natural gas and petrochemical feedstocks such as propylene had inflated and remained volatile, with more material P&L effects expected from Q2 onward; it increased its full-year raw-material-inflation outlook to low-to-mid single digits.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The Q1 moderation is not a basis for a Home Depot margin benefit because coatings manufacturers and a retailer recognize costs differently. The later cost outlook is a prospective shared risk, not a quantified Q1 Home Depot EPS mapping; it is therefore excluded from the add-on.
  SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-First-Quarter-Financial-Results/
  SOURCE: https://s2.q4cdn.com/918177852/files/doc_events/2026/Apr/28/CORRECTEDTRANSCRIPT_TheSherwin-WilliamsCo-SHW-USQ12026EarningsCall28-April-202610_00AMET.pdf
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-First-Quarter-Financial-Results/
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/events-and-presentations/event-details/2026/Sherwin-Williams-First-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-Conference-Call-2026-1mMMAgU3g5/default.aspx
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://s2.q4cdn.com/918177852/files/doc_events/2026/Apr/28/CORRECTEDTRANSCRIPT_TheSherwin-WilliamsCo-SHW-USQ12026EarningsCall28-April-202610_00AMET.pdf

COMPARABLE: Fortune Brands Innovations, Inc. (FBIN)
REPORT DATE: 2026-05-07
REPORTED PERIOD: Q1 2026
WHY COMPARABLE: Fortune Brands supplies directly overlapping residential categories: Moen faucets and water products, Therma-Tru and Larson doors, Fiberon decking and railing, and Yale residential security. Those categories share Home Depot exposure to repair-and-remodel demand, housing affordability, consumer confidence, commodity inflation, freight and tariffs.
SHARED EXPOSURES:
- Residential repair-and-remodel demand
- Housing affordability and consumer sentiment
- Plumbing, doors, decking and outdoor-project demand
- Commodity, freight and tariff costs
- Pricing realization
TRANSFERABLE EARNINGS POINTS:
- More cautious consumer sentiment and increased commodity inflation worsened the company's market and financial outlook. [MACRO, NEGATIVE]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: Fortune Brands updated 2026 guidance to reflect sales in line with the market and cited a more uncertain external environment from increased commodity inflation and more cautious consumer sentiment. It changed full-year net-sales guidance from flat to up 2% to down low single digits, reduced EPS-before-charges/gains guidance from $3.35-$3.65 to $3.00-$3.30, and reduced operating-margin-before-charges/gains guidance by 100 basis points at the midpoint.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: This is directionally negative for Home Depot's discretionary project demand and potentially its merchandise-cost environment. However, Fortune Brands also identified inconsistent execution in Q1, and its release does not isolate the macro contribution to actual Q1 sales or profit. The company is therefore retained as qualitative corroboration but excluded from the quantitative add-on.
  SOURCE: https://ir.fbin.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fortune-brands-innovations-announces-first-quarter-results
- Quarterly category demand was mixed across residential water, outdoors and security products. [INDUSTRY, MIXED]
  IMPACT ON COMPARABLE: First-quarter total sales decreased 2.1% to $1,011.3m. Water Innovations sales declined 0.3%, Outdoors sales declined 3.4%, and Security sales declined 6.0%. Total operating margin before charges/gains declined 200 basis points to 11.1%.
  READ-THROUGH TO TARGET: The category pattern reinforces weaker discretionary outdoor and home-project demand, but it cannot be cleanly transferred to Home Depot because the company specifically cited execution issues and has a different channel mix. No numerical Home Depot sales, comp-sales or EPS effect is inferred from these declines.
  SOURCE: https://ir.fbin.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fortune-brands-innovations-announces-first-quarter-results
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://ir.fbin.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fortune-brands-innovations-announces-first-quarter-results
EARNINGS SOURCE: https://ir.fbin.com/events/event-details/q1-2026-earnings-call

PRELIMINARY COMPARABLE-ONLY METRIC ADD-ONS:
- Net sales: 0 USDm (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: $0m. The qualifying comparables provide directional/category signals but no compliant Home Depot Q1 net-sales base, category-sales mix, or conversion coefficient. Under the instruction to use only qualifying comparables in the adjustment and evidence, converting the -0.2 percentage-point comparable-sales signal into dollars would require an unsupported Home Depot-specific sales base; the defensible add-on is therefore zero.
  ASSUMPTION: No target-company sales base, target category mix, or absolute-sales forecast is imported.
  ASSUMPTION: Comparable evidence is used only to assess direction and relative same-store demand.
  ASSUMPTION: A zero is preferable to an ungrounded dollar scaling under the stated comparable-only constraint.
  SOURCE: https://ir.flooranddecor.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/296/floor-decor-holdings-inc-announces-first-quarter-fiscal
  SOURCE: https://s21.q4cdn.com/596588259/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/transcript/MAS-Q1-2026-Transcript.pdf
  SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-First-Quarter-Financial-Results/
  SOURCE: https://ir.fbin.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fortune-brands-innovations-announces-first-quarter-results
- Adjusted diluted EPS: 0 USD / share (NEUTRAL)
  CALCULATION: $0.00/share. The peer releases show mixed pricing/demand and input-cost signals, but they do not establish a Home Depot-specific incremental gross-margin, operating-expense, tax-rate or diluted-share conversion. Masco and Sherwin-Williams are manufacturers with different price/cost timing, and Fortune Brands' profit change includes execution issues expressly excluded from the mapping. Accordingly, no defensible comparable-only per-share adjustment is available.
  ASSUMPTION: No target-company margin, tax or diluted-share assumptions are imported.
  ASSUMPTION: Tariff, commodity and freight comments are not converted into Home Depot EPS because peer pass-through, sourcing and recognition timing differ.
  ASSUMPTION: Peer-specific execution effects and non-comparable accounting effects are excluded.
  SOURCE: https://s21.q4cdn.com/596588259/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/transcript/MAS-Q1-2026-Transcript.pdf
  SOURCE: https://s2.q4cdn.com/918177852/files/doc_events/2026/Apr/28/CORRECTEDTRANSCRIPT_TheSherwin-WilliamsCo-SHW-USQ12026EarningsCall28-April-202610_00AMET.pdf
  SOURCE: https://ir.fbin.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fortune-brands-innovations-announces-first-quarter-results
  SOURCE: https://ir.flooranddecor.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/296/floor-decor-holdings-inc-announces-first-quarter-fiscal
- Comparable sales, total company: -0.2 % (DECREASE)
  CALCULATION: -0.2 percentage points, rounded from -0.23 points. Arithmetic mean of three deliberately attenuated, directly overlapping demand signals: [Floor & Decor comparable-store sales -3.7% × 20% cross-category transmission = -0.74 points] + [Masco DIY-paint low-single-digit decline, midpoint assumed -2.0% × 10% = -0.20 points] + [Sherwin-Williams Paint Stores same-store sales +2.4% × 10% = +0.24 points]; (-0.74 - 0.20 + 0.24) / 3 = -0.233 points. Fortune Brands is excluded from the calculation because its release identifies inconsistent execution alongside the macro environment, preventing a clean shared-demand isolation.
  ASSUMPTION: The Masco phrase 'low single-digit decrease' is represented by a -2.0% midpoint solely for transparent directional scaling.
  ASSUMPTION: The 20% Floor & Decor attenuation reflects its specialty, big-ticket flooring concentration versus Home Depot's materially broader maintenance, repair, pro and category mix.
  ASSUMPTION: The 10% Masco and Sherwin-Williams attenuations reflect manufacturer/dedicated-store channel differences and the narrower paint-category exposure relative to Home Depot total company.
  ASSUMPTION: This is an incremental same-season comparable signal, not a Home Depot absolute comparable-sales forecast.
  ASSUMPTION: No target-company news, post-2026-05-18 facts, analyst estimates, share-price reactions or non-qualifying earnings releases are used.
  SOURCE: https://ir.flooranddecor.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/296/floor-decor-holdings-inc-announces-first-quarter-fiscal
  SOURCE: https://s21.q4cdn.com/596588259/files/doc_earnings/2026/q1/transcript/MAS-Q1-2026-Transcript.pdf
  SOURCE: https://investors.sherwin-williams.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/The-Sherwin-Williams-Company-Reports-2026-First-Quarter-Financial-Results/

events.title: Lowe’s issues cautious 2026 outlook amid delayed major DIY projects
events.summary: Reuters reported that Lowe’s forecast 2026 comparable sales ranging from flat to up 2%. Lowe’s cited stagnant housing, guarded consumer spending, tariffs and customers delaying major kitchen, flooring and other costly DIY projects. The report noted that Home Depot had retained its annual outlook while expecting housing-market pressure to persist.
source_headlines: Lowe’s provides cautious 2026 outlook as DIY customers delay costly remodels

events.title: February existing-home sales rise 1.7% but remain below prior-year level
events.summary: AP reported that U.S. existing-home sales increased 1.7% month over month in February to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.09 million, as buyers responded to easing mortgage rates. Sales remained 1.4% below February 2025, and the national median price reached a February record.
source_headlines: Existing U.S. home sales rose 1.7% in February, though remained below the prior-year pace

events.title: Home Depot plans 12 new U.S. stores for 2026
events.summary: Home Depot announced plans to add 12 stores across eight U.S. states during 2026, representing more than 1.6 million square feet. The planned locations are intended to support same-day delivery and pickup and will include dedicated Pro teams, tool-rental capacity and larger storage areas for online-order fulfillment.
source_headlines: The Home Depot adds 12 U.S. stores and more than 1.6 million square feet of retail space for 2026

events.title: Federal Reserve maintains federal-funds target range at 3.50%–3.75% in March
events.summary: The FOMC maintained the federal-funds target range at 3.50% to 3.75%, effective March 19, 2026.
source_headlines: Federal Reserve holds the federal-funds target range at 3.50%–3.75%

events.title: U.S. broadens aluminum, steel and copper tariff regimes
events.summary: A White House proclamation applied duties to the full customs value of covered aluminum, steel, copper and derivative imports beginning April 6, 2026. It imposed a 50% additional ad valorem duty on many listed articles, subject to specified lower rates and exclusions for certain products.
source_headlines: U.S. strengthens aluminum, steel and copper tariff regimes, including 50% duties for covered products

events.title: March existing-home sales fall 3.6%; NAR reduces 2026 forecast
events.summary: AP reported that U.S. existing-home sales fell 3.6% in March to a 3.98 million annualized rate, the slowest pace in nine months. The article cited higher mortgage rates as energy prices increased and reported that the National Association of Realtors reduced its 2026 existing-home-sales growth forecast to 4% from 14%.
source_headlines: Existing U.S. home sales fell 3.6% in March; NAR cut its 2026 sales forecast

events.title: Home Depot acquires SIMPL Automation for distribution-center automation
events.summary: Home Depot acquired SIMPL Automation, a warehouse-automation and technology company. Home Depot said a pilot at its Locust Grove, Georgia, distribution center resulted in faster pick speeds and cycle times with fewer product touches, and said SIMPL’s storage-and-retrieval technology could increase the density and availability of high-demand inventory. Financial terms were not disclosed in the source material.
source_headlines: The Home Depot acquires SIMPL Automation to expand distribution-center automation

events.title: Federal Reserve again maintains federal-funds target range at 3.50%–3.75%
events.summary: The FOMC again left the federal-funds target range unchanged at 3.50% to 3.75%. Its statement said economic activity was expanding at a solid pace, inflation was elevated in part because of the recent increase in global energy prices, and Middle East developments had increased economic uncertainty.
source_headlines: Federal Reserve again holds the federal-funds target range at 3.50%–3.75%, citing elevated energy-price-driven inflation

events.title: SRS Distribution completes acquisition of Mingledorff’s
events.summary: SRS Distribution, a Home Depot subsidiary, completed its acquisition of Mingledorff’s, an HVAC equipment, parts and supplies distributor serving residential and commercial customers through 42 locations in five Southeastern states. Home Depot stated that HVAC distribution adds an approximately $100 billion addressable market and raises its stated total addressable market to about $1.2 trillion. Financial terms were not disclosed.
source_headlines: SRS Distribution completes acquisition of HVAC distributor Mingledorff’s

events.title: April retail sales slow; building-material and garden sales rise 0.1%
events.summary: AP, citing Commerce Department data, reported that U.S. retail sales rose 0.5% in April, following a 1.6% increase in March. Building-material and garden-equipment sales increased 0.1%. The article reported that higher gasoline prices were consuming more household income, with the average regular-gas price at $4.53 per gallon, up $1.35 from a year earlier.
source_headlines: April U.S. retail sales slowed as higher gasoline costs squeezed discretionary budgets; building-material and garden sales rose only 0.1%

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Forecast Q1 FY2026 net sales = prior reported Q4 FY2025 sales $38,198m + GUIDANCE $3,053m + E6 ($60m) + E10 ($60m) + all other events $0m + COMPARABLES $0m = $41,131m; total change = +$2,933m. Period alignment: management guidance is FY2026; Q1 is forecast from the comparable prior-year Q1 sales base of $39,856m × (1 + FY midpoint total-sales guidance of 3.5%) = $41,251m, rather than applying FY growth mechanically to the preceding Q4. The $120m subsequent-data reduction is recognized in Q1 because March housing data and April retail-sales data fall within or immediately inform the May 3 Q1 cut-off.

event_contributions.affected_line: sales volume, store/branch additions and acquisition mix
event_contributions.transmission_path: FY total-sales guidance -> comparable prior-year Q1 seasonal sales base -> Q1 net sales. The midpoint includes guided contributions from GMS, new stores, SRS branches and tuck-ins, while the 1.0% comparable-sales midpoint represents underlying same-store demand.
assumptions: FY2026 guidance midpoint is 3.5% total-sales growth.
Q1 FY2025 net sales of $39,856m is the appropriate standalone-quarter seasonal base; it is not interchangeable with the preceding Q4's $38,198m.
Applying the FY midpoint to the comparable Q1 is a central phasing assumption; GMS and branch/store growth are already included in management guidance.
event_contributions.calculation: Q1 guided sales = $39,856m × 1.035 = $41,251m. GUIDANCE change versus prior reported Q4 sales = $41,251m - $38,198m = +$3,053m.

event_contributions.affected_line: sales volume in large discretionary DIY projects
event_contributions.transmission_path: Delayed kitchen, flooring and other costly projects could reduce transactions and ticket -> net sales. No incremental Q1 adjustment is taken because management's FY comparable-sales range explicitly already embeds persistent housing, affordability and consumer-demand pressure.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Forecast Q1 FY2026 adjusted diluted EPS = $3.61. Change versus prior reported Q4 FY2025 adjusted EPS of $2.72 = +$0.89. Contribution arithmetic: GUIDANCE +$0.91 + E6 ($0.01) + E10 ($0.01) + all other events $0.00 + COMPARABLES $0.00 = +$0.89. The EPS forecast is derived from the consolidated income-statement bridge, not copied from EPS guidance.

event_contributions.affected_line: sales, operating margin, net interest expense, tax and acquired-intangible amortization
event_contributions.transmission_path: FY sales, operating-margin, tax-rate and interest-expense guidance -> phased Q1 revenue and operating income -> pretax income -> net income -> adjusted net income -> diluted EPS.
assumptions: Q1 guided revenue before later demand updates is $41,251m.

Q1 GAAP operating margin is set at 12.70%, modestly above the FY 12.4%-12.6% midpoint due to Q1 seasonality but below the FY2025 Q1 reported margin; it reconciles to a guided FY margin near the midpoint after lower-margin acquisition mix.
Q1 net nonoperating expense is $620m, phased from $2.3bn FY interest-expense guidance with Q1 debt-cost seasonality.
Tax rate is the guided 24.3%.
After-tax acquired-intangible amortization is $120m in Q1, consistent with the approximately $0.50 FY adjusted-EPS exclusion and a Q1-weighted quarterly allocation.
Diluted shares are held at 994m, consistent with Q1 FY2025 reported diluted weighted-average shares.
event_contributions.calculation: Guided Q1 operating income = $41,251m × 12.70% = $5,239m. Pretax income = $5,239m - $620m = $4,619m. GAAP net income = $4,619m × (1 - 24.3%) = $3,497m. Adjusted net income = $3,497m + $120m = $3,617m. Guided adjusted EPS = $3,617m / 994m = $3.64, rounded; GUIDANCE contribution versus $2.72 = +$0.91 after retaining unrounded bridge values.

earnings_bridge.calculation: Linked Q1 FY2026 net sales = $41,131m. Operating income = $41,131m × 12.65% + $0m = $5,203.1m. Pretax income = $5,203.1m - $620m + $0m = $4,583.1m. GAAP net income = $4,583.1m × (1 - 24.3%) = $3,469.4m. Adjusted net income = $3,469.4m + $120m after-tax acquired-intangible-amortization exclusion = $3,589.4m. Adjusted diluted EPS = $3,589.4m / 994m shares × 1 = $3.61.
assumptions: The 12.65% Q1 GAAP operating margin is a seasonally aligned estimate around the FY 12.4%-12.6% guided range, reflecting acquisition mix and the $120m combined E6/E10 sales reduction.

The $620m Q1 net nonoperating expense is the Q1 allocation of approximately $2.3bn FY net interest expense, informed by Q1 FY2025's $591m interest-and-other-net expense and modestly higher FY guidance.

The $120m adjustment is the after-tax Q1 allocation of the approximately $0.50 FY acquired-intangible-amortization adjusted-EPS exclusion; it does not add back revenue generated by acquired intangibles.
Shares are held at the Q1 FY2025 diluted weighted-average level of 994m because no pre-cutoff repurchase or dilution change supports a different Q1 estimate.

metric_impacts.metric_total_calculation: Forecast Q1 FY2026 total-company comparable sales = prior reported Q4 FY2025 comparable sales 0.4% + GUIDANCE 0.6 percentage points + E6 (-0.05 points) + E10 (-0.05 points) + COMPARABLES (-0.10 points) + all other events 0.00 points = 0.8%. Therefore projected change versus the previous reported actual is +0.4 percentage points. The FY guidance midpoint is phased to Q1 as 1.0% because management described demand as persistently pressured with no housing catalyst, so no acceleration within the year is assumed.

assumptions: FY comparable-sales guidance midpoint is 1.0%.
Q1 is set at the FY midpoint, rather than pro-rating a growth rate, because comparable sales is already a rate and management supplied no quarterly phasing or inflection catalyst.
Prior reported Q4 comparable sales were 0.4%.
event_contributions.calculation: Guidance-implied Q1 comp = 1.0%. GUIDANCE change versus previous reported 0.4% = +0.60 percentage points.
